facts.raw_span: A 76-year-old woman presented with macular edema
The patient was treated with 2 intravitreal anti–vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) injections
At 3 months after presentation, her macular edema was completely resolved, without recurrence
No specific physical examination findings were reported in the case
At 6 months: No abnormality observed
At 12 months: En face OCT revealed hyperreflective tissues starting to proliferate on retinal vessels
At 12 months: OCTA B-scan showed pyramid-shaped proliferations
At 15 months: Hyperreflective tissues increased in size with angiogenic sprouts showing flow signals extending vertically
At 18 months: Development observed in area of preexisting proliferation
At 21 months: Enlarged horizontal structures along retina surface
Performed at 21 months showing dendritic vascular-like structures
Figure 1: Sequential development over 1 year showing progression from normal vessels to proliferation

concepts.why: The patient's OCTA and Fluorescein Angiography findings, including hyperreflective tissues, pyramid-shaped proliferations, and dendritic vascular-like structures, are consistent with neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

The patient's OCTA findings, including hyperreflective tissues and pyramid-shaped proliferations, are consistent with retinal angiomatous proliferation, a subtype of neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

The patient's OCTA findings, including hyperreflective tissues and pyramid-shaped proliferations, are consistent with type 3 neovascularization, a subtype of neovascular age-related macular degeneration.
The patient's OCTA and Fluorescein Angiography findings, including hyperreflective tissues and dendritic vascular-like structures, are consistent with macular neovascularization.

The patient's OCTA findings, including hyperreflective tissues and pyramid-shaped proliferations, are consistent with choroidal neovascularization, a subtype of neovascular age-related macular degeneration.

rationales.F06: Hyperreflective tissues on retinal vessels suggest neovascularization, more typical of Retinal Angiomatous Proliferation and Macular Neovascularization.
rationales.F07: Pyramid-shaped proliferations on OCTA B-scan are characteristic of neovascularization, supporting Retinal Angiomatous Proliferation and Macular Neovascularization.
rationales.F08: Angiogenic sprouts with flow signals indicate active neovascularization, consistent with Retinal Angiomatous Proliferation and Macular Neovascularization.
rationales.F09: Development in areas of preexisting proliferation suggests progression of neovascularization, supporting Retinal Angiomatous Proliferation and Macular Neovascularization.
rationales.F10: Enlarged horizontal structures along the retina surface are indicative of neovascularization, more typical of Retinal Angiomatous Proliferation and Macular Neovascularization.
rationales.F11: Dendritic vascular-like structures on fluorescein angiography are characteristic of neovascularization, supporting Retinal Angiomatous Proliferation and Macular Neovascularization.
rationales.F12: Sequential development showing progression from normal vessels to proliferation is consistent with neovascularization, supporting Retinal Angiomatous Proliferation and Macular Neovascularization.
